The `renv` package is used for R package management at **project level**. It can help trace packages versions and keep environments **reproducible** sharing R projects with others or deploying projects to a server.

- Each project has its own isolated environment (a folder shown as `renv/library`).

- Each project has a `renv.lock` tracking package versions.

- renv caches packages globally hence no duplication downloads of the same package could happen.

# How to start


::: {.callout-tip}

Simply run `renv::init()` in a R console. It will create a `renv/library` folder, a `.Rprofile` file, and a `renv.lock` file.

:::


::: {.callout-caution}

Do not commit the `renv/library` folder to version control.

:::

# Add a package

When adding a new package, it will go to the project's isolated library folder.


::: {.callout-note}

Remember to use `renv::snapshot()` to add a new package to the `renv.lock` file.

Only used packages are added to the `renv.lock` file, not every installed package is actively used in a R project.

:::

# Check sync status

Use `renv::status()` to check if all packages are captured in the `renv.lock` file or not.

# Restore an environment

Start with `renv::status()`, if installed packages and the `renv.lock` file is out of sync, you can use `renv::restore()` to update/install required packages as tracked by the `renv.lock` file.


::: {.callout-note}

If a package is already used by another project, then the `renv::restore()` command would use the cached package/library rather than downloading it again. This saves disk space and speeds up restore process.

:::

# Online course

Posit has introduced an [online how-to course](https://academy.posit.co/getting-started-with-renv) of using `renv`.
